words.gloss: those who do not possess (firmness in action)

literal: Whatever other firmness even when attained, those who do not possess firmness in action, the world will not value.
translation: Even if they possess every other kind of strength, the world will not respect those who lack firmness in action.
modern: எவ்வளவு வலிமைகளைப் பெற்றிருந்த போதிலும், செய்யும் செயலில் உறுதி இல்லாதவர்களை இந்த உலகம் மதிக்காது.
explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme importance of resoluteness in action. The term 'enait-tiṭpam' refers to any other kind of strength, such as wealth, physical power, or intellectual capacity. The poet asserts that even if one attains all these other strengths, they are of no value if one lacks 'vinai-tiṭpam', which is firmness and determination in executing a task. The world will ultimately disregard and fail to respect those who cannot carry out their actions with unwavering resolve.
